public_comment.topic: Objected to the board's public rationale for not reappointing a conservation commission member, saying the board did not fact-check his voting record before citing it as a reason.

minutes.headline: Board voted 4-1 to send a letter pressing school/finance committees to communicate better ahead of budget season
minutes.summary: The Select Board handled routine business (license renewals, resignations, a town-manager report) then spent most of the meeting on two policy rewrites (special events, appointments), a letter to the Governor on state aid, and a letter to the tri-board on communication after friction at the recent special town meeting. It also discussed unresolved special-town-meeting items -- Kids Kingdom's design/relocation, a water-billing rate increase, and a mailer-postcard bylaw change -- without final decisions.

budget_items.topic: DMH Jail and Arrest Diversion Program grant (police, with Lancaster)
budget_items.what_was_said: Town manager reported the grant funds a clinician (via Open Sky Community Services) to assist police with mental-health crises; a board member asked the amount and got a different-sounding figure in response.
Town manager reported the FY26 tax rate has been officially set by DLS; third-quarter actual tax bills are being prepared.

budget_items.topic: Town Hall access control project change order
budget_items.what_was_said: A change order is needed because the library, teen center and adult activity center are on a separate network; the shortfall will be covered from the Wallace Park resurfacing project, which came in under budget.

budget_items.topic: State/local aid figures cited in draft letter to the Governor
budget_items.what_was_said: Draft letter to the Governor cites MMA figures on the share of municipal revenue from state aid, the decline in unrestricted aid, flat Chapter 90 funding since 2012, and an example earmark amount, as part of an FY27 local-aid advocacy letter.

budget_items.topic: Water billing accounts / rate increase (11 account holders, Fitchburg dispute)
budget_items.what_was_said: Town manager said a rate increase will be needed for the 11 affected water accounts and that not all recent payments to Fitchburg were applied correctly; a suggestion to ask Fitchburg to pause interest is being pursued.

Town manager said an RFP for a full design (funded by town meeting) shouldn't go out without a clear scope, and that a cheap conceptual sketch could be done first rather than spending the larger design sum on something that may not be built.
An accounts payable warrant in this amount was presented to the board.

budget_items.topic: Forestry/Chapter land rollback taxes, 100 Hobbit Street
budget_items.what_was_said: Board of Assessors report: a 44-acre chapter-land parcel sold in October for this amount, and the town is pursuing rollback taxes retroactive up to five years plus interest.

transfers.description: Shortfall on the access-control project change order, taken from the Wallace Park resurfacing project (completed under budget)
transfers.outcome: discussed only, presented as town manager's plan

decisions.decision: Board will wait one more week (to Dec 16) to see which license applicants come into compliance, then consider a contingent vote on remaining renewals; a special meeting may be scheduled in late December if needed.

Board leaning toward substantially rewriting or scrapping the special events policy, likely splitting it into a large-event policy and a routine/small-event policy, and removing regulation of private-property events; town counsel to be consulted on legality.
Board will explore digitizing volunteer applications (e.g., via a Microsoft Form feeding a spreadsheet) while keeping a paper option.

Board agreed to a series of edits to the draft appointment policy: remove fixed May 25th deadline, require a vote of the full board (not one member) to trigger interviews for an appointed body, move annual-report due date from fixed November to 'as requested,' and add training requirements to the policy.
Board will ask town counsel for input on whether a select board bylaw is even needed and how other towns handle it before recommending changes to the Bylaw Review Committee.

Board leaning toward sending a letter to the school committee affirming the school committee's care, custody and control of Kids Kingdom, paired with a rough conceptual site sketch to inform further discussion, rather than issuing it unilaterally.

what_happened.line: The board voted 4-1 to send the school and finance committees a letter pressing for better communication ahead of budget season, after friction at the recent special town meeting.
The board began rewriting its special events and appointment policies, including splitting event rules by size and loosening fixed deadlines for board appointments, without a final vote.
The board held off on remaining delinquent license renewals for one more week and may call a special meeting in late December if applicants have not come into compliance.
The board discussed but did not decide two unresolved items from the special town meeting: a water-billing rate increase for affected accounts and the Kids Kingdom playground redesign.
A resident used public comment to object that the board's stated reason for not reappointing a conservation commission member was not fact-checked.

why_it_matters: The tri-board letter could change how budget information reaches the school committee and finance committee before residents are asked to vote on next year's school budget.
A water-billing rate increase would land on the bills of the affected account holders, and the license-renewal delay affects local businesses awaiting town approval.
The Kids Kingdom redesign and the appointment-policy changes touch a town recreation project and the process by which residents get seated on town boards.
watch_next: December 16 review of remaining license-renewal compliance, with a possible special meeting in late December
Finalized tri-board communication letter and revised special events and appointment policies coming back to the board
